clue.text: Largely recommend imbibing a drink

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece takes the other inside it
largely means most of the word, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to recommend a course is to advocate it

explanation.surface: Someone mostly urges a guest to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' trims ADVOCATE to ADVOCAT, and 'imbibing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made with eggs, sugar and brandy.

clue.text: From whom one can trace descent — or ascent, alternatively

definitions.text: From whom one can trace descent

indicators.note: alternatively suggests another arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A genealogist muses that family lines can be traced downward or upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is the person from whom a line of family descends.

clue.text: Extremely weak signal

parts.note: very means extremely
light can mean weak, as in a light drink

explanation.surface: A signal so faint it barely registers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is a coloured flare fired from a pistol as a signal, named after its inventor.

clue.text: Obscure Conservative, aggressive and noisy

parts.note: loud describes both a brash, aggressive manner and noise

explanation.surface: A forgettable Tory backbencher who is pushy and shouty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective describing the politician but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloud an issue is to make it murky or unclear.

clue.text: Old expert upset people of intelligence

parts.note: arch means cunning or knowing, as an expert is

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: An elderly specialist upsets clever people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CIA into AIC; 'people of intelligence' are spies, not brainy folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to a much earlier period, antiquated.

clue.text: Ruffian's father in pain

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in places the parent inside the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a dull pain
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A thug's dad is suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: An apache was a Paris street thug of the early twentieth century, so the word names a violent hoodlum.

clue.text: I have a trunk, and intend to be abroad by end of June

parts.note: to plan is to intend
etre is French for 'to be', so it is 'to be' in a foreign tongue

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A traveller with luggage means to be overseas by late June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests luggage, but it is the tree's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a tree, and every tree stands on a trunk.

clue.text: Become irritated and hot in restaurant

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
H abbreviates hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A diner gets annoyed and overheated while eating out.
explanation.definitionFit: To chafe is to feel impatience or annoyance.

clue.text: Property in French art gallery

parts.note: es is an old French word for 'in', as in docteur es lettres
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A building held in a Parisian gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is land or possessions that someone owns.

clue.text: Press fail to win in court

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: to fail to win is to lose

explanation.surface: Reporters see a litigant lose a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests newspapers; it means a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is an old word for a cupboard, especially for linen.

clue.text: Motor travel can be a burden

parts.note: a motor is an informal British word for a car
to travel is to go

explanation.surface: Driving can be a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is a load carried by a vessel, a weight borne.

clue.text: Stop Lily getting lame

parts.note: the calla is the arum lily
halt is an old word for lame

explanation.surface: Lily's limp forces her to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To call a halt is an idiom for ordering something to cease.

clue.text: Musical youth

definitions.meaning: A 1954 British stage musical by Julian Slade
the phrase means one's green, inexperienced younger years

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Cleopatra coined the phrase for her inexperienced younger years, and it later titled a long-running London show.

clue.text: Take part in seventh race, possibly

indicators.note: take part in tells you to take a portion of the next word

explanation.surface: Joining the seventh race at a meeting, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is one example of a sporting contest, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: No cigar could be produced without chemicals

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A smoker is told no cigar can be made without additives.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic farming avoids artificial fertilisers and pesticides.

clue.text: Rotten centre in a drupe

indicators.note: rotten fruit falls apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stone fruit has gone bad at its core.
explanation.definitionFit: A drupe is a fleshy fruit with a stone, like a peach or a smooth-skinned peach variety.

clue.text: Abusive language from artist at centre of main movement

indicators.note: at centre of puts the artist in the middle of the other word

parts.note: the main is the sea, whose movement is the tide
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter caught up in a political movement swears violently.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of denunciation.

clue.text: Medium? First of definitions is "moderate"

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to temper is to moderate

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry claims a psychic's first meaning is 'moderate'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic; it is a medium for painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a water-based paint, a medium for decorating walls.

clue.text: Hit around. I will drop

indicators.note: around has the first piece go round the second

parts.note: to paste is to thrash or hit
I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: After a beating, someone says they will collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray 'IS'; the page prints only 'Hit around. I will drop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a small boiled sweet, like a lozenge.

clue.text: Capital punishment

definitions.meaning: the ... were a wooden frame in which offenders were pilloried

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both shares held as funds and the old wooden frame for punishing offenders.

clue.text: Small lake comes into view

indicators.note: comes into means one piece enters the other

parts.note: a sight is a view
L abbreviates lake on maps

explanation.surface: A little lake appears on the horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight means slender or small in degree.

clue.text: Tea includes different kind of bun

indicators.note: includes means one word holds the other inside

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
else means other or different

explanation.surface: Afternoon tea features an unusual sort of bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea bun is a sticky currant bun rolled in a spiral, named after the London district.

clue.text: Provide finishing touch, mostly column heading …

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: to cap it all is to add the final touch

explanation.surface: An editor tops off a feature with a headline over a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last L from CAP IT ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital is the carved top of an architectural column.

clue.text: … that is followed by inventory in old book

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for 'that is to say'
a roll is a list or register

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a list follows in an ancient volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Before bound books, writings were kept on a rolled parchment.

clue.text: Sinuous mover needs firm support

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a support garment

explanation.surface: A dancer with curves needs a well-made bra.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobra is a snake, which moves with winding curves.

clue.text: Stay at the wicket — stick there

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to keep batting is to ...
a short stick, as in a relay

explanation.definitionFit: The two-word cricket phrase for continuing an innings also spells the word for a short staff.

clue.text: Irritable, but apt in time to become composed

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Someone tetchy is advised to calm down in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like 'calm' but signals the anagram; 'but' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An impatient person is restless and easily annoyed.

clue.text: Join group climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine

explanation.surface: Sign up with a mountaineering party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting piece of a woodworking joint.

clue.text: Speak up as fox gets killed

parts.note: to fox someone is to baffle or outwit them
hit is slang for killed, as by a gangland hit

explanation.surface: A hunt reports that the fox has been dispatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fox' reads as the animal but is a verb; 'as' and 'gets' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Out with it is an idiom urging someone to say what they are holding back.

clue.text: Starts from near East Pakistan, and lands in this country?

indicators.note: starts from means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A traveller arriving near East Pakistan wonders which land this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan kingdom close to the former East Pakistan, now Bangladesh.

clue.text: Cut into melted candle

indicators.note: melted wax loses its shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone carved into a softened candle.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance a boil is to pierce it with a blade.

clue.text: Countryman without name lies around idling

annotationWithheld.why: Countryman without name lies around idling (8): FLANERIE; no countryman word less N combines with any reading of 'lies around' to give these letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Countryman without name lies around idling
